questions.subject: CNN
questions.question: Explain the difference between pooling layers and feature maps in CNN.
questions.ideal_answer: pooling layers and feature maps differ in several ways: pooling layers is spatial dimensionality reduction (works by translation invariance) whereas feature maps is convolution output channels (works by hierarchical feature learning). pooling layers is typically used for max pooling, average pooling, while feature maps is used for edges -> textures -> patterns -> objects. questions.subject: CNN
questions.question: Explain the difference between receptive field and ResNet in CNN.
questions.ideal_answer: receptive field and ResNet differ in several ways: receptive field is input region influencing neuron (works by effective area of influence) whereas ResNet is residual network (works by skip connection architecture). receptive field is typically used for stacked convolutions increase RF, while ResNet is used for solving vanishing gradient in deep networks. Example demonstrating receptive field: RF = RF_prev + (kernel - 1) * stride_product. Example demonstrating ResNet: F(x) + x identity mapping.
